THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING,
THROUGH PHYSICAL HEARING/VIDEO CONFERENCE, THIS DAY T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA, J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

In this appeal the appellants have challenged the judgment dated 19.10.2017 passed in MVC No.882 of 2015 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Chincholi (Hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal' for short), seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. The parties will be referred with respect to their status before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.
3. Briefly stated the facts are that, 1st petitioner is the wife, 2nd, 3rd and 4th petitioners are the children, the 5th petitioner is the mother of one Shankar @ Shanakrappa, the deceased.
The deceased was killed in a road accident on 04.05.2015 at about 07:30 p.m.
He was traveling in an Auto Rickshaw bearing No.KA-32/B-1644.
It hit against Babool tree near the land of one Chandrakanth Mali Patil on Sulepeth Kodampalli Road, near Kodampalli Village.
Petitioners approached the Tribunal seeking compensation of Rs.46,70,000/-.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.
The Tribunal awarded Rs.9,27,000/- with 6% interest.

4. Heard arguments of Sri Harshavardhan R. Malipatil, learned counsel for the appellants and Sri Sudharshan M., learned counsel for the 2nd respondent.
5.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that, the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- per month by agriculture, but the Tribunal has considered only Rs.6,000/-, not considered future prospects and the compensation to be paid under conventional heads is not sufficient and they sought for reassessment and enhancement.
6.
Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company contended that since there is no proof of income and the accident was of the year 2015, the Tribunal has rightly taken Rs.6,000/-.
That apart the compensation under the conventional heads has already been settled and sought for assessment of the compensation by applying the settled principles.
7. We have given our anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of the parties and perused the records.
8. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of accident, death of the deceased in the accident and the petitioners as dependents to claim compensation.

As regards income of the deceased, since he was an agriculturist and the accident took place in the year 2015, we are of the opinion that notional income ought to have taken as Rs.8,000/- per month and accordingly we hold that amount to be the income of the deceased.

sentences.text: Ex.P5 P.M. report confirms the age of the deceased as 50 on the date of accident.

As per the principles laid down in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others - 2017 ACJ 680 loss of future prospects in case of self employee shall be 25% for the age between 40 to 50.

sentences.text:
10. If all these factors are taken into consideration, the assessment of loss of dependency would be:
Rs.8,000/- (Income of the deceased) + Rs.2,000/- (25% Future Prospects) =
Rs.10,000/- per month.
As there are five dependents, 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal expenses of deceased, then it comes to Rs.7,500/- and if it is multiplied by 12 and 13, it comes to Rs.11,70,000/-.

11. As regards to conventional heads, the deceased left with wife, three children and mother, hence towards loss of consortium to wife and loss of love and affection to the children and mother,
Rs.40,000/- each and towards loss of estate and funeral expenses Rs.15,000/- each is assessed.
Thus, the total compensation comes to Rs.11,70,000/- + Rs.2,30,000/- = Rs.14,00,000/- as against Rs.9,27,000/- awarded by the Tribunal, thereby there is enhancement of Rs.4,73,000/-.
It is the just compensation the petitioners are entitled to in the facts and circumstances of the case.
The appeal deserves to be partly allowed accordingly.

12. In the result, the following:
ORDER
The appeal is allowed in part.
The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified.
The petitioners are entitled to total compensation of Rs.14,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per year as against Rs.9,27,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Thereby enhancement of Rs.4,73,000/-.
Rest of the judgment and award of the Tribunal is kept intact.
Office is directed to transfer the amount if any in deposit, to the Tribunal.
